title: Follow Athaliah's rise and fall in Jerusalem

jerusalem.name: Jerusalem
jerusalem.text: The capital of Judah, where Athaliah seized power and ruled for six years (2 Kings 11:3). The temple and the royal palace stood close together on the city's northern ridge. The marker is on today's Temple Mount.

samaria.name: Samaria
samaria.text: The capital of the northern kingdom of Israel under Omri and Ahab. Athaliah belonged to this royal house: 2 Kings 8:18 calls Jehoram's wife a daughter of Ahab, and 2 Kings 8:26 calls Athaliah a granddaughter of Omri.

jezreel.name: Jezreel
jezreel.text: A royal city of Israel on a ridge above the Jezreel Valley, identified with Tel Jezreel. Athaliah's son Ahaziah was visiting the wounded King Joram here when Jehu rebelled (2 Kings 8:29; 9:16).

ibleam.name: Ibleam
ibleam.text: Jehu's men wounded Ahaziah on the way up to Gur near Ibleam (2 Kings 9:27). Ibleam is usually identified with Khirbet Bel'ameh, south of modern Jenin.

megiddo.name: Megiddo
megiddo.text: Ahaziah escaped as far as Megiddo and died there. His servants carried his body to Jerusalem by chariot and buried him in the City of David (2 Kings 9:27–28).

telaviv.name: Tel Aviv
telaviv.text: Modern city on the Mediterranean coast, shown for orientation.

chapters.title: A princess of Ahab's house in Jerusalem
chapters.html:
Athaliah came from the northern royal house of Omri and Ahab, whose capital was Samaria. She married Jehoram, king of Judah, and Kings says he followed the ways of Ahab's family.

After Jehoram died, their son Ahaziah became king in Jerusalem at age twenty-two. He reigned only one year, and 2 Chronicles 22:3 says his mother encouraged him in doing wrong.
facts: The marriage sealed an alliance between Judah and Israel. A generation later, Jerusalem had a temple of Baal with its own priest, Mattan (2 Kings 11:18).
The name Athaliah is usually understood to include a short form of the divine name Yahweh, even though she promoted Baal worship.

chapters.title: Her son dies in Jehu's coup
chapters.html:
Ahaziah went north to visit King Joram of Israel, Ahab's son, who was recovering from wounds at Jezreel. There the army commander Jehu rebelled and killed Joram.

Ahaziah fled, but Jehu's men wounded him near Ibleam, and he died at Megiddo. His body was brought back to Jerusalem. The royal house of Ahab was being destroyed, and in Judah the throne suddenly stood empty.
facts: The Tel Dan Stele, an Aramaic inscription from the ninth century BC, mentions the "house of David." Many scholars read it as an Aramean king claiming the deaths of Joram and Ahaziah, which the Bible credits to Jehu.
From Jezreel to Megiddo is about 9 miles (14 km) in a straight line across the Jezreel Valley.

chapters.title: Athaliah seizes the throne
chapters.html:
When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she set out to destroy the whole royal family of Judah. Ahaziah's sister Jehosheba rescued the infant Joash, one of the king's sons, and hid him with his nurse in a bedroom.

Joash stayed hidden at the temple for six years while Athaliah ruled the land. Chronicles adds that Jehosheba was the wife of Jehoiada the priest.
facts: Athaliah is the only woman the Bible records as ruling Judah or Israel as monarch in her own right.
The dates of her reign depend on which chronology of the kings is used, so they are approximate.

chapters.title: The coup at the temple
chapters.html:
In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest brought the commanders and guards into the temple and showed them the young king. They crowned Joash, and the people clapped and shouted, "Long live the king!"

Athaliah heard the noise, came to the temple and saw the king by the pillar. She was led out between the ranks and put to death where the horses enter the palace grounds. The people then tore down the temple of Baal.
facts: Joash was seven years old when he became king (2 Kings 11:21), and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem.
Jehoiada had the guards take Athaliah out of the temple area first, because she was not to be put to death in the temple of the Lord (2 Kings 11:15).
